extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, respondents and counsel in USPTO disciplinary proceedings; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria used by the USPTO Administrative Law Judge/OED to evaluate practitioner misconduct, service/default, complaint sufficiency, and to determine sanctions in disciplinary proceedings before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may serve a complaint on a respondent by mailing a copy by 'Express Mail,' first-class mail, or any delivery service that provides ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery to a respondent who is a registered practitioner at the address provided to OED pursuant to § 11.11, or if the respondent is not registered, to the respondent's last address known to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must be to the address of record or last known address; exhibits showing delivery receipts (e.g., delivery to household member) establish proper service. Proper service is a prerequisite to finding default when respondent fails to answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify OED of contact information (37 C.F.R. § 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney or agent registered to appear before the PTO must notify the Director of his or her postal office address, e-mail addresses, business telephone number, and every change to any of said addresses or telephone numbers within thirty days of the date of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to maintain accurate contact information can affect service and the ability to participate in proceedings; service to the address provided satisfies service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer timing and default (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An answer to a complaint is due thirty days after the complaint is served (the first business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday). Failure to file a timely answer constitutes admission of the allegations in the complaint and a default judgment may be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent does not file an answer, the tribunal may enter default without providing additional time to respond to a motion for default; default admission means allegations are taken as true for purposes of disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response period for motions (37 C.F.R. § 11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer determines the time period in which a response to a motion must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In motions for default where the respondent has not answered or otherwise appeared, it is not necessary to allow time for a response to the motion; nonetheless the hearing officer may give an extended period but is not required to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint sufficiency requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.34(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must fairly inform the respondent of any grounds for discipline and give a plain and concise description of the respondent's alleged grounds for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts that merely allege the respondent engaged in 'the acts or omissions described expressly or impliedly in the Complaint' are unacceptably vague and do not meet § 11.34 requirements; each count must articulate specific factual allegations so respondent is fairly informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misappropriation / failure to remit client funds (Rule 10.23(a),(b) via 10.23(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule proscribes misappropriation of funds or failure to properly or timely remit funds received by a practitioner from a client to pay a PTO fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting and receiving client funds for patent issue/publication fees and attorney fees, but failing to forward the client funds to the PTO and retaining them, constitutes a violation. The decision applies this to funds received for Notice of Allowance fees that were not remitted, resulting in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (Rule 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not transmitting client funds intended for PTO fees and retaining them may be characterized as dishonest or deceitful conduct under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform client of significant PTO correspondence (Rule 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule proscribes failure to inform a client of significant correspondence received from the PTO where the correspondence was received by respondent and a reasonable practitioner would believe the client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice of Abandonment (and similar PTO correspondence having a significant effect on an application) triggers an obligation to notify the client; failing to do so violates this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of legal matter entrusted (Rule 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule proscribes neglect of a legal matter entrusted to a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing a client's patent application to become abandoned through failure to pay necessary fees, failing to respond to client communications, and failing to inform the client of abandonment constitutes neglect under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to return client funds/property on request (Rule 10.112(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule proscribes failure to pay or deliver to a client as requested client funds and properties in the practitioner's possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaining unearned attorney fees and client-paid PTO fees and failing to return the client's files after written requests violates this rule; repeated ignored requests aggravate the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Other' conduct limitations for Count pleading (Rule 10.23(b)(6) interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be 'other' conduct within the scope of Section 10.23(b)(6), conduct must not be prohibited by Section 10.23(b)(1)-(5); counts based merely on 'acts or omissions described' are too vague to sustain separate liability under (b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complaint cannot rely on boilerplate 'other' language when the factual allegations are identical to other enumerated counts; specificity is required to charge 'other' conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions factors (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining appropriate sanction the tribunal must consider: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to a client, the public, the legal system, or the profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused by the misconduct; and (4) existence of aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four factors guide the choice and severity of discipline (suspension, exclusion, etc.). The decision applies these factors to find intentional misconduct, actual injury (costs to revive application), and aggravating factors supporting suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ABA Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions as guidance (Standards § 9.22, § 9.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ABA Standards delineate aggravating and mitigating factors relevant to sanctions: § 9.22 lists aggravating factors (e.g., pattern of misconduct, multiple offenses, refusal to acknowledge wrongful conduct, substantial experience, indifference to restitution); § 9.32 lists mitigating factors (e.g., absence of prior disciplinary record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribunal may cite ABA Standards to identify aggravating and mitigating factors; presence of multiple aggravators (pattern, experience, refusal to make restitution) supports harsher sanction while limited mitigating factors (no prior record) are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on tribunal authority to order restitution (35 U.S.C. § 32 constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tribunal has previously held that it lacks authority to enter an order of restitution by virtue of limitations set forth in 35 U.S.C. § 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a complainant may seek restitution, the ALJ/tribunal may be constrained from ordering monetary restitution and must instead choose sanctions within its statutory authority (e.g., suspension/exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of disciplinary proceedings and sanction severity guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of attorney disciplinary proceedings is to protect the public and the justice system from lawyers derelict in professional duties; abandonment of a case or client after being paid is a significant violation that can justify severe sanctions (suspension, exclusion, or disbarment depending on circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past sanctions in comparable cases (including disbarment/exclusion) inform appropriate discipline; suspension for a substantial period (e.g., three years) may be appropriate where respondent defaults and the record cannot be further developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO prosecution obligation re: Notice of Allowance fees and abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Allowance informs that patent issue and publication fees must be paid within three months from the date of the notice or the application will be regarded as abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners who receive client funds to pay issue/publication fees must remit them timely or otherwise advise client; failure to remit leading to abandonment is a basis for misconduct findings under Part 10 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and timeline (37 C.F.R. § 11.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal from an initial decision must be filed with the USPTO within 30 days after the date of the initial decision and must include exceptions to the ALJ's decision and supporting reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely appeal in accordance with § 11.55 will be deemed acceptance of the initial decision and a waiver of rights to further administrative and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary findings and post-discipline obligations (§§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The facts and circumstances of disciplinary proceedings shall be published in the PTO's official publication; disciplined practitioners are subject to responsibilities set forth in § 11.58 and may petition for reinstatement under § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order notifies respondent of post-discipline responsibilities and reinstatement procedures; publication of the decision is mandatory and part of the sanctioning process.
